problem:
A siren on a fixed post in still air sounds a steady note of frequency 1500 Hz along a straight road. The flat rear panel of a lorry, facing the post, drives directly away from it at a constant 6 m/s and sends the sound straight back, with no change of frequency in its own rest frame. A recorder on a trolley faces the lorry, so that it picks up the reflected sound; the trolley starts beside the post and runs directly away from the lorry along the same line at a constant 9 m/s. Take the speed of sound in the still air as 343 m/s. A toolbox stands on the trolley beside the recorder when the trolley sets off.

By how much does the frequency of the reflected sound that the recorder picks up lie below the frequency of the note?

A warming cabinet stands beside the enclosure, and no heat passes between the cabinet and the enclosure.
